hero.title: Thin Ice: The Arctic Sea Ice Maximum of 2026 and the World That Depends On It
hero.excerpt: On March 15, the Arctic sea ice reached its 2026 maximum: 14.29 million km², the lowest in the 48-year satellite record. An area twice the size of Texas that never froze. The ice is telling its story.

hero.title: The Briefing Before the Landing: What Expedition Leaders Can Teach Corporate Managers
hero.excerpt: Decisions made at sea level, far from support, reveal a discipline of communication and trust that boardrooms rarely have to practice. Here is what the ice teaches about leading under pressure.

hero.title: Scramble for the North Pole: Continental Shelf Claims, Geopolitics and the Future of the Arctic Council
hero.excerpt: Three nations claim the same seabed. As the Arctic thaws, the pressure to draw new lines on an old map is quietly reshaping the politics of the far north.

hero.title: The Colour of Ice: What Blue, White, Green and Black Tell Us About a Glacier’s Life
hero.excerpt: Ice is never simply white. Its hues are a diary of pressure, age and origin — a language you can learn to read from the deck of a ship or the foot of a calving face.

hero.title: Russia’s Arctic Silence: What Happens to Circumpolar Science When Half the Arctic Is Off-Limits
hero.excerpt: When cooperation freezes, the data freezes with it. The gaps left in the record have consequences that reach far beyond any single border.
